fidelity: F2a — Physics-Lumped High-Pressure Water Scrubbing (Henry's-law absorption, transient column ODE)
source: Bauer et al. (2013) Bioresour. Technol. 122:145 'Biogas upgrading — Review of commercial technologies'; Sun et al. (2015) Renew. Sustain. Energy Rev. 51:521 'Selection of appropriate biogas upgrading technology'; Sander (2015) Atmos. Chem. Phys. 15:4399 (Henry's-law compilation); Cussler (2009) Diffusion: Mass Transfer in Fluid Systems

unit.name: High-Pressure Water Scrubber (HPWS) absorption column — lumped

V_liquid.note: Liquid hold-up volume in packed absorption column

L_water.note: Scrubbing water recirculation flow (~180 m3/h) at design biogas load

P_col.note: Column operating pressure (Bauer 2013: 6-10 bar typical for HPWS)

T_col.note: Column temperature (10C; cold water favours CO2 solubility)

kLa_CO2.note: Volumetric liquid-side mass-transfer coeff for CO2 (random packing); gives NTU~7-8

H_cp_CO2.note: Henry solubility H^cp of CO2 at 298.15K (Sander 2015, =0.034 mol/(L.atm))

H_cp_CH4.note: Henry solubility H^cp of CH4 at 298.15K (Sander 2015, =0.0014 mol/(L.atm))

selectivity_CH4_CO2.note: kLa_CH4/kLa_CO2 ratio; CH4 absorbs far slower (low solubility -> ~1.8% slip)
